refuted_vulnerabilities.description: TimezoneMixin.get_tzname() converts self.tzinfo to a string without validating that it is a trusted datetime.tzinfo instance. Database backend operations interpolate the resulting timezone name into SQL (for example, AT TIME ZONE '<tzname>') without parameterization or escaping. If an attacker can supply tzinfo, including a string or an object whose tzname() returns SQL metacharacters, the generated query can be altered.
refuted_vulnerabilities.impact: Potential SQL injection through Extract(), Trunc(), TruncDate(), and TruncTime() when tzinfo is attacker-controlled, allowing data exfiltration, modification, or other database compromise.
refuted_vulnerabilities.remediation: Validate tzinfo when the expression is constructed: require None or a genuine datetime.tzinfo instance, reject strings and arbitrary objects, and validate the resulting timezone name against a strict allowlist before it reaches database operations.
refuted_vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept: With USE_TZ=True, instantiate Extract or Trunc with a user-controlled tzinfo value whose string representation or tzname() contains SQL quote characters. get_tzname() returns that value, and the backend interpolates it into the generated SQL.

verification.reason: The reported code only resolves a developer-supplied ORM expression argument (self.tzinfo) through Django's internal timezone helper; there is no request, form, query, or other untrusted external input boundary in this path.
verification.mitigating_control: Trusted internal context / no external untrusted input boundary

taint_path.description: Constructor accepts an unvalidated tzinfo value.
tzinfo is converted to a string without type or content validation.
The unvalidated timezone name is interpolated into generated SQL.
